name: Photo library, add only
plain: Saves a photo or video into the library without being able to read any of it.
meaning: Lets an app drop images in (camera, scanner, meme maker) with no view of what is already stored, a far smaller disclosure than reading the roll.

android.prompt_ui: None: MediaStore insert into the app's own pending item shows no prompt
android.persistence: Item remains; app may modify only files it created
android.revocation: n/a (the app can only touch its own items)
android.note: Scoped storage (API 29) means writing your own media needs no permission

ios.revocation: Settings > Privacy & Security > Photos > Add Photos Only
ios.store_policy: App Review 5.1.1: ask for the smallest access
ios.note: Add-only still allows saving with the older UIImageWriteToSavedPhotosAlbum path

limits.headline: Can save new photos and videos to your library, but cannot look at what is there
limits.user_action: You tap Save photo, Save to gallery or Download image
can: Save a new photo or video into your library
Save the app's own media on Android with no prompt
Ask for add only permission on iPhone, shown as Allow or Don't Allow
Keep saved items in your gallery
cannot: See any existing photo or video in your library
List albums or count your photos
Delete or change the photos already there
Save on iPhone without your tap on the add only prompt
limits.differs: Android needs no permission for the app's own new media. iPhone shows an add only prompt.

story.what_it_is: Lets an app save a photo or video to your library without seeing what is already there.

marketing.name: Add only photo access
marketing.pitch: Developer guide: apps can ask for add only access, so they can save photos without reading the library.

story.for_you: A pop up asks to add photos only. If you say yes, a camera app can save a picture but cannot look at your other photos. It is a much smaller share than full access.
story.for_makers: Makers need it to save results like scans, edits and downloads. Asking for add only keeps trust high and is easier to get approved.

use_cases.example: A camera app saves new pictures to your library and cannot see old ones.
A document scanner saves a scan as a photo in your library.
A meme or sticker maker saves a finished image to share.
A game saves a screenshot of your best score.
A retailer saves a QR code or coupon image to your photos.
An AR app saves a photo of a 3D object in your room.
A video downloader saves a clip you chose.

risks: Still adds clutter to your library
story.android_note: Android apps can save through MediaStore with no permission on recent versions.
story.ios_note: A separate add only choice in the Photos permission.

technical_bounds: Read back of the saved item is not guaranteed on iOS add-only
Cannot enumerate other apps' media on either platform

history.change: Scoped storage: no permission to write own media
